title: Week 05 · Session 1 — Multimodal AI: Same Idea, Different Medium
description: A 75-minute active learning session on multimodal AI, creativity, communication, audience, accessibility, and human revision. Students compare how the same idea changes across text, image, audio, and video, then create and improve a multimodal communication artifact they can reuse as evidence for AI Tool Exploration Journal #2.

steps.label: MAKE THE CALL
steps.title: Same message. Which format would make you act?
steps.lead: A campus event changes location one hour before it starts. What would get your attention fastest?
steps.studentTask: Choose the format you think would work best for you. Then be ready to explain what that format can do that the others cannot.
steps.roomInstruction: Choose the format most likely to get your attention and help you act.

runbook.openWith: Today is about a simple idea: changing the medium can change the meaning, usefulness, and accessibility of a message.
runbook.whyMatters: Students begin with their own communication habits before defining multimodal AI.
runbook.ask: Why did you choose that format? What would it do better than the others?
runbook.listenFor: Speed, attention, clarity, emotion, convenience, accessibility, context.
runbook.ifTheySay: Video is always better → ask whether they would still prefer video in a quiet library, while driving, or with poor bandwidth.
runbook.ifQuiet: Ask who would choose differently if the message were urgent, private, or complicated.
runbook.pushFurther: Does a better format depend on the message, the audience, or both?
runbook.sayDuringReveal: There is no universal best medium. The right choice depends on purpose, audience, context, and what people need to do next.
runbook.landHere: Communication quality is not just about what is said. It is also about how the message reaches someone.
runbook.transition: Now let’s name what AI changes when it can work across several kinds of media.
runbook.studentDoes: Chooses a preferred communication format and explains why.
runbook.askNext: What changes when the same idea moves from text to image, audio, or video?
runbook.watchFor: Students treating format preference as a universal rule.
runbook.ifStuck: Give the same message in two imagined settings: walking between classes versus studying quietly.
runbook.advanceWhen: Students can name at least two tradeoffs between formats.

steps.label: MULTIMODAL
steps.title: AI can work across more than one kind of information.
steps.lead: Text, images, audio, video, and documents can become inputs, outputs, or both.
steps.studentTask: Phones down. Follow the four examples and identify what goes in, what comes out, and what a human still needs to judge.
steps.roomInstruction: TEXT · IMAGE · AUDIO · VIDEO — input, output, or both.
steps.visualAccent: MULTIMODAL = more than one mode of information
steps.visualCaption: The same AI system may read an image, answer in text, generate a visual, or turn a transcript into a script.

runbook.openWith: Multimodal does not mean “AI that makes pictures.” It means working across different forms of information.
runbook.whyMatters: Students need a simple conceptual definition before experimenting.
runbook.ask: Which of these examples changes both the input and the output format?
runbook.listenFor: Photo to text, text to image, audio to transcript, transcript to video plan.
runbook.ifTheySay: Multimodal just means multimedia → distinguish media content from an AI system interpreting or generating across modalities.
runbook.ifQuiet: Use a phone camera example: image goes in, text description comes out.
runbook.pushFurther: What might be lost when one mode is translated into another?
runbook.sayDuringReveal: Every transformation creates choices. Some choices are technical. Others are about audience, meaning, accuracy, accessibility, and judgment.
runbook.landHere: Multimodal AI transforms information across modes; humans still decide what the transformation should preserve.
runbook.transition: Let’s see what gets lost when we confuse what a system can see with what it can infer.
runbook.askNext: What could be lost or distorted when a message changes format?
runbook.watchFor: Students assuming an output preserves all meaning from the input.
runbook.ifStuck: Ask what a photo communicates that a transcript cannot, and vice versa.
runbook.advanceWhen: Students can explain multimodal AI in plain language.

steps.label: SEE
steps.title: A picture can show evidence without explaining the whole story.
steps.lead: Imagine a photo of a student staring at a laptop at 2:00 AM. What can an AI actually observe?
choices: The student is looking at a laptop
The student has an exam tomorrow
steps.studentTask: Choose the ONE statement that is directly supported by the image description. Separate observation from inference.
steps.roomInstruction: OBSERVED or INFERRED? Choose the one statement supported directly by the evidence.
steps.visualCaption: Visual information can be useful while still leaving intent, emotion, and context uncertain.

runbook.openWith: Multimodal AI can interpret images, but image interpretation still involves inference.
runbook.whyMatters: This connects Week 5 to the course habit of separating evidence from assumption.
runbook.ask: Which statement could you defend from the evidence alone?
runbook.listenFor: Looking at laptop is observable; stress, procrastination, and exam status require additional context.
runbook.ifTheySay: The facial expression proves stress → ask whether one expression has only one possible explanation.
runbook.ifQuiet: Ask which statement could be verified by another person looking at the same image.
runbook.pushFurther: What additional information would you need before making one of the inferences?
runbook.sayDuringReveal: Images feel rich, but they do not automatically provide intention, identity, emotion, or context.
runbook.landHere: Multimodal input gives us more evidence, not unlimited understanding.
runbook.transition: Now we move from interpreting media to transforming it.
runbook.studentDoes: Separates visible evidence from inferred meaning.
runbook.askNext: What additional context would make one of the inferences more defensible?
runbook.watchFor: Students treating image detail as certainty about mental state or intent.
runbook.ifStuck: Ask what a camera could literally record.
runbook.advanceWhen: Students can explain why only one option is directly observed.

steps.label: LIVE TRANSFORM
steps.title: Watch one idea change shape.
steps.lead: We will take one plain message and transform it for different audiences and formats.
steps.studentTask: Watch the transformation. For each version, identify what became clearer, what disappeared, and what still needs human review.
steps.roomInstruction: SAME IDEA → DIFFERENT FORMAT → DIFFERENT DESIGN CHOICES
steps.visualCaption: The goal is not to generate more content. The goal is to communicate the idea better for a specific audience.

runbook.openWith: I am going to use AI as a communication partner, not as an answer machine.
runbook.whyMatters: Students see the quality bar before they begin their own experiment.
runbook.ask: What should stay constant across every version? What should change?
runbook.listenFor: Core meaning stays; length, tone, imagery, pacing, structure, and accessibility may change.
runbook.ifTheySay: The AI version looks polished so it is better → ask whether it preserved the intended meaning and audience.
runbook.ifQuiet: Use the shared message: “Before using AI for schoolwork, check course expectations, verify important outputs, protect private information, and keep the final decision yours.”
runbook.pushFurther: Which format introduces the greatest risk of oversimplifying the message?
runbook.sayDuringReveal: A strong transformation preserves the important idea while making deliberate choices for the audience and medium.
runbook.landHere: Good multimodal work is designed, not merely generated.
runbook.transition: Now you will run the same experiment yourselves.
runbook.say: Use this shared message for the demo: “Before using AI for schoolwork, check course expectations, verify important outputs, protect private information, and keep the final decision yours.” Ask AI to create a short text message, a visual concept, a 20-second audio script, and a three-shot video storyboard for first-year students.
runbook.studentDoes: Observes a live multimodal transformation and evaluates what changes.
runbook.askNext: Which version would you actually use, and what would you revise first?
runbook.watchFor: Students focusing only on aesthetic polish.
runbook.ifStuck: Compare the exact wording and ask what each version emphasizes or omits.
runbook.advanceWhen: Students can name one gain and one loss created by changing format.

steps.label: CREATE
steps.title: Build two versions of the same idea.
steps.lead: Use AI to communicate one useful message in two different formats.
choices: STUDENT LIFE — explain a useful study or campus habit
INFORMATICS — explain a technology concept to a first-year student
AI LITERACY — explain one responsible-use principle from this course
steps.studentTask: Work in pairs. Choose one message and one intended audience. Create TWO versions using different formats: text, visual/image, audio script, or video storyboard. Save your prompts and outputs. Use only low-risk, non-private information.
steps.roomInstruction: PAIR CHALLENGE · ONE IDEA · TWO FORMATS · ONE AUDIENCE
steps.visualCaption: Save the prompt, both outputs, and one note about what changed between formats.

runbook.openWith: This is the part worth saving. You are creating evidence for Journal #2 while you experiment.
runbook.whyMatters: The activity directly produces prompts, outputs, revisions, and evaluation evidence for the weekly deliverable.
runbook.ask: Who is your audience? What should they understand or do after seeing your message?
runbook.pause: About 14 minutes building + 6 minutes comparison notes.
runbook.listenFor: Audience, purpose, format, accessibility, preserved meaning, revision choices.
runbook.ifTheySay: We do not know what to make → suggest explaining phishing, passwords, cloud storage, AI verification, or a study habit in plain language.
runbook.ifQuiet: Circulate and ask each pair: what is the one idea both versions must preserve?
runbook.pushFurther: Ask the AI to revise one version for a different audience. What changes?
runbook.sayDuringReveal: Do not upload private, sensitive, copyrighted, employer-owned, student-identifying, health, or financial information. Use your own low-risk content or a fictional example.
runbook.landHere: The evidence is not just what AI generated; it is what you changed and why.
runbook.transition: Before we decide which version is better, we need two filters: accessibility and ownership.
runbook.studentDoes: Creates two multimodal communication versions and saves journal-ready evidence.
runbook.askNext: What changed because the medium changed?
runbook.watchFor: Students generating two artifacts without defining an audience or purpose.
runbook.ifStuck: Have the pair use the same message but change only the medium.
runbook.advanceWhen: Pairs have two versions plus a short comparison note.

steps.label: CHECK
steps.title: Polished is not the same as responsible.
steps.lead: Before sharing AI-generated media, what should you check?
choices: ACCURACY — does it preserve the intended meaning?
ACCESSIBILITY — can people use it in more than one way?
OWNERSHIP — do I have the right to use the material?
ALL THREE — responsible communication needs all of them
steps.studentTask: Choose the strongest answer, then identify one concrete check your pair can apply to its own work.
steps.visualCaption: Captions, transcripts, alt text, attribution, copyright, and factual review are part of the communication task.

runbook.openWith: Generative tools make it easy to create something that looks finished before it is actually ready.
runbook.whyMatters: Students need a practical responsible-use checkpoint for multimodal work.
runbook.ask: What would you check before putting your artifact in public?
runbook.listenFor: Factual accuracy, alt text, captions/transcripts, attribution, source ownership, audience fit.
runbook.ifTheySay: The AI made it, so copyright does not matter → ask what source material, logos, images, styles, or other protected content may still be involved.
runbook.ifQuiet: Ask what a student using a screen reader would need from a visual-only artifact.
runbook.pushFurther: Could an artifact be accurate but still inaccessible? Could it be accessible but legally or ethically questionable?
runbook.sayDuringReveal: Responsible multimodal communication requires more than a correct sentence. The format itself creates obligations.
runbook.landHere: Accuracy, accessibility, and ownership are part of quality.
runbook.transition: Use those checks to improve one of your outputs now.
runbook.studentDoes: Evaluates multimodal work with three responsible-use checks.
runbook.askNext: Which of the three checks changes your artifact the most?
runbook.watchFor: Students treating accessibility as an optional add-on.
runbook.ifStuck: Give examples: image + alt text; audio + transcript; video + captions.
runbook.advanceWhen: Students can name a concrete check for each category.

steps.label: IMPROVE
steps.title: Revise one version for a real person.
steps.lead: Make one deliberate change because of audience, accessibility, accuracy, or ownership.
steps.studentTask: Choose one of your two versions. Revise it once. Then submit a short note: “I changed ___ because ___.” Save the before/after versions for Journal #2.
steps.visualCaption: Human revision is part of the multimodal workflow.

runbook.openWith: The first output is not the product. Revision is where your judgment becomes visible.
runbook.whyMatters: Students create before/after evidence that demonstrates human decision-making rather than passive AI use.
runbook.ask: What did you change, and what evidence justified that change?
runbook.listenFor: Audience fit, readability, accuracy, captioning, alt text, tone, length, attribution, removal of misleading content.
runbook.ifTheySay: We liked the first version → require one improvement based on a specific user need or responsible-use check.
runbook.ifQuiet: Offer the stem: “A first-year student might ___, so we changed ___.”
runbook.pushFurther: Would the same revision help every audience?
runbook.sayDuringReveal: The point is not to prove AI can make media. The point is to show that you can make a responsible communication decision about AI-generated media.
runbook.landHere: Human judgment is visible in the revision.
runbook.transition: Finish by capturing the rule you want to remember.
runbook.studentDoes: Revises one artifact and records the reason for the change.
runbook.askNext: What changed because of your audience rather than because of the AI tool?
runbook.ifStuck: Choose one of the three checks: accuracy, accessibility, or ownership.
runbook.advanceWhen: Pairs have a before/after artifact and a one-sentence rationale.

steps.label: EXIT
steps.title: What changed when the medium changed?
steps.lead: Turn today into one sentence you can reuse in Journal #2.
steps.studentTask: Complete: “Changing the medium changed ___, and a human still needed to ___.” Save one prompt, one output, and one revision from today for Journal #2.
steps.roomInstruction: CHANGING THE MEDIUM CHANGED ___ · A HUMAN STILL NEEDED TO ___
steps.visualAccent: Format changes communication. Judgment still belongs to people.
steps.visualCaption: Save your prompt · output · revision · rationale.

runbook.openWith: Before you leave, turn the experiment into one rule you can carry forward.
runbook.whyMatters: The reflection converts class activity into reusable portfolio and Journal #2 evidence.
runbook.ask: What did the medium change? What still required human judgment?
runbook.listenFor: Audience, emphasis, accessibility, clarity, accuracy, ownership, revision.
runbook.ifTheySay: The AI made it more creative → ask what specifically changed and whether that helped the intended audience.
runbook.ifQuiet: Display the sentence stem and ask them to choose one concrete change.
runbook.pushFurther: Which artifact from today best proves your claim?
runbook.sayDuringReveal: Multimodal AI gives us more ways to create. AI literacy means knowing which form fits the purpose, what gets lost, and what still needs human revision.
runbook.landHere: Design the communication. Check the evidence. Revise for people.
runbook.watchFor: Generic statements without a specific human action.
runbook.ifStuck: Prompt: What did you verify, caption, rewrite, remove, or explain?
runbook.advanceWhen: Students have submitted and saved one artifact.
